#+property: header-args :tangle "~/.emacs.d/init.el" :results silent
#+startup: content indent

* Introduction

This file generates the `~/.emacs.d/init.el` configuration
file I use for emacs. It's maintained in Org Mode using
Literate Coding (Documentation prose around indiviudual code 
snippets. The snippets get combined into the config file
without the surrounding text.)

* Notes

** Updating 

The contents of the source blocks in this file are
automatcially tangled to the `~/.emacs.d/init.el`
file when it's saved (if you need to tangle it
manually for some reason, you can use `C-c C-v t`).

In lots of cases you can jsut evaluate individual
functions to add them to the mix. However, things
getting removed might require a restart to
see the effect take place.

* AWS Functions

** check-for-projectile-tab-names
*** Overview

Check to see if there's a .tab-name file and set the
tab-bar-mode tab to it if there is one. This is
done to define unique tab names when necessary
to allow treemacs to associate the proper directories
with each project. (It's only required if the default
name for the tab would conflict with the directory
name from another project.) 

The second half of the mapping is done via:
`treemacs-edit-workspaces`

*** Setup

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
  (defun aws/check-for-projectile-tab-names ()
    "Check for a .tab-name file to set the tab-bar-mode tab with"
    (let ((path (aws/file-exists-in-project ".tab-name")))
      (when path
        (tab-bar-rename-tab 
         (with-temp-buffer
  	 (insert-file path)
  	 (string-trim (buffer-string)))))))
  (add-hook 'projectile-after-switch-project-hook #'aws/check-for-projectile-tab-names)
#+end_src

*** Overview

[] Create a new blog entry.

*** Setup

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
  (defun my/create-blog-entry ()
    (interactive)
    (let* ((time (current-time))
  	 (id (my/time-to-base32 time))
  	 (id-dir (my/id-to-dir id))
  	 (dir-path (expand-file-name id-dir "~/workshop/al9000.com/content/blog"))
  	 (file-path (concat dir-path "/index.html")))
      (unless (file-directory-p dir-path)
        (make-directory dir-path t))
      (if (file-exists-p file-path)
  	(find-file file-path)
        (with-temp-buffer
  	(insert-file-contents "/Users/alan/workshop/al9000.com/content/blog/template.inc.html")
  	(goto-char (point-min))
  	(while (search-forward "TIMESTAMP_STRING" nil t)
  	  (replace-match (format-time-string "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%:z" time)))
  	(goto-char (point-min))
  	(while (search-forward "ID_STRING" nil t)
  	  (replace-match id-dir t))
  	(write-region (point-min) (point-max) file-path nil 'silent))
        (find-file file-path)))
    )

** save-all

*** Overview 

Function to save all files that need it without
attempting to save files that don't or buffers
that aren't attached to files. 

*** Setup

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(defun aws/save-all ()
    "save files with changes (skipping buffers without associated files)"
    (interactive)
    (dolist (buf (buffer-list))
      (with-current-buffer buf
        (when (and buffer-file-name
  		 (buffer-modified-p))
  	(save-buffer)))))
#+end_src

** create-file-with-mkdir
*** Overview

[x] Open a buffer pointing at the requested file
location.

[x] Make any direcotires necessary to place the file.

[x] The buffer is empty (and the file isn't created
yet) if the file does not exist.

[x] The buffer has the contents of the file if
the file exists. 

[x] Return `t` if file is created or already exists.

[] Return `nil` if there's a problem.

[] Log messages if there are errors. 

*** Setup

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
  (defun my/create-file-with-mkdir (path)
    "Create a new file at the path and open it. Make dirs if necessary."
    (interactive)
    (let ((dir (file-name-parent-directory path)))
      (unless (file-directory-p dir)
        (message "Making directory: %s" dir)
        (make-directory dir t))
      (unless (file-exists-p path) 
        (message "Making file: %s" path))
      (find-file path)
      )
    t)
#+end_src

** time-to-base32
*** Overview

Converts a time object to base32
with second level precision.
The initial use case if for IDs
for blog posts. 

*** Setup

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
  (require 'iso8601)
  (require 'parse-time)
  (defun my/time-to-base32 (time)
    (interactive)
   "Convert a timestamp to base32 with second level percision
  using the Crockford base32 character set with lower case letters."
    (let* ((crockford-base32 "0123456789abcdefghjkmnpqrstvwxyz")
  	 (ts (logand (time-convert time 'integer)
  		     (1- (ash 1 40))))
  	 (chars nil))
      (dotimes (_ 8)
        (push (aref crockford-base32 (logand ts 31)) chars)
        (setq ts (ash ts -5)))
      (concat chars)))
#+end_src

** Prevent overtaking windows
*** Overview

  Set up Occur to display in the current 
  window instead of taking over another 
  window. (This can be used for other things
  as well if they take over other windows. 
  The format is to start with a regex for 
  matching the buffer, then functions to 
  use for it.)
  NOTE: This is based off the examples from
  this video:
  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1-UIzYPn38s 

  You can use `or` for the `display-buffer-alist` 
  instead of making matchers for each buffer. 
  The example I saw in this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1-UIzYPn38s
  didn't work as expected, but I probably copied
  the code incrorrectly. Didn't bother to troubleshoot
  since I don't need it right now. 

*** Setup

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
  (setq display-buffer-alist
        '((
  	 ;; Buffer name matcher
  	 "\\*Occur\\*"
  	 ;; Functions to run
  	 ;; These functions prevent the 
  	 ;; Occur buffer from taking over the 
  	 ;; other windows with open buffers in them.
  	 (display-buffer-reuse-mode-window
  	  display-buffer-below-selected)
  	 ;; Parameters
  	 ;; This ensures that if you open a new 
  	 ;; buffer while occur is open the new 
  	 ;; buffer doesn't load into the occur window. 
  	 (dedicated . t)
  	 ;; Call the function to select the window 
  	 ;; instead of staying in the calling window. 
  	 (body-function . aws/select-window)
  	 ;; Don't add a mode line to the window. 
  	 (window-parameters . ((mode-line-format . none))))))
#+end_src

*** Setup

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
  (defun aws/file-exists-in-project (filename)
    "Return the full path to FILENAME in the current project root if it exists, else nil."
    (let ((root (projectile-project-root)))
      (when root
        (let ((path (expand-file-name filename root)))
          (when (file-exists-p path)
            path)))))
#+end_src

#+end_src


Not using this right now, but it's a way to use
tab to make a selection (with nothing pre-selected)
and return to activate it. Saving it now to
experiment with later. 

#+begin_src emacs-lisp :tangle no 
  (use-package corfu
    :custom
    (corfu-preselect 'prompt)            ;; don't preselect anything 
    (corfu-cycle t)                      ;; optional: cycle through candidates
    :bind
    (:map corfu-map
  	("TAB" . corfu-next)           ;; Move to next candidate with tab
          ([tab] . corfu-next)           ;; Move to next candidate with tab
          ("S-TAB" . corfu-previous)     ;; Move to prev candidate with shift-tab
          ([backtab] . corfu-previous)   ;; Move to prev candidate with shift-tab
          ("RET" . my/corfu-ret))        ;; Return uses selection
    :init
    (global-corfu-mode))

  (defun my/corfu-ret ()
    "Insert the selected candidate if one is chosen, otherwise newline."
    (interactive)
    (if (>= corfu--index 0)
        ;; a candidate is actively selected -> insert it
        (corfu-insert)
      ;; nothing selected -> behave like normal RET
      (progn
        (corfu-quit)
        (call-interactively (key-binding (kbd "RET"))))))

#+end_src

  (evil-define-key '(normal) 'global (kbd ",") 'hydra-main-menu/body)
  (evil-define-key '(normal insert) 'global (kbd "C-S-d") 'tab-bar-switch-to-prev-tab)
  (evil-define-key '(normal insert) 'global (kbd "C-d") 'tab-line-switch-to-prev-tab)
  (evil-define-key '(normal insert) 'global (kbd "C-S-f") 'tab-bar-switch-to-next-tab)
  (evil-define-key '(normal insert) 'global (kbd "C-f") 'tab-line-switch-to-next-tab)
  (evil-define-key '(normal insert) 'global (kbd "C-s") 'aws/save-all)
  (evil-define-key
    '(normal insert)
    'global (kbd "C-w")
    '(lambda ()
       (interactive)
       (aws/save-all)
       (kill-buffer (current-buffer))
       :wk "save all and close current"))
  (evil-define-key '(normal insert) 'global (kbd "C-e") 'treemacs-select-window)
#+end_src

* Package: hydra
** Overview 

- Hydra makes a menu of hotkeys you can use in a
  repetative fashion (e.g. hitting `C-d` multiple times
  moves to the previous project tab each time)

- Link: https://github.com/abo-abo/hydra

- REMINDER: Don't use `:color` in the main `defhydra` call.
  It prevents closing the hydra window in some cases. 

- The `:exit t` closes the hydra window after
the command is run. 

- The `:hint nil` in the main defun sets up so the
  keys are duplicated on the last line.

** Setup the menu

Initialize the package

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
    (use-package hydra)
#+end_src

Create the main menu

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
  (defhydra hydra-main-menu (:hint nil)
    "
  [ c ] close file tab 
  [ C ] close project tab
  [ t ] tangle file 
  [ r ] run org source block
  [ 7 ] decrease font size
  [ 8 ] increase font size 
  "

    ("c" tab-line-close-tab :exit t)
    ("C" tab-bar-close-tab :exit t)
    ("t" org-babel-tangle :exit t)
    ("r" aws/run-source-block :exit t)
    ("7" aws/decrease-font-size)
    ("8" aws/increase-font-size)
    ) 
#+end_src

Create the file menu

#+begin_src emacs-lisp 
  (defhydra hydra-file-menu (:hint nil)
    "
  [ b ] open buffer 
  [ d ] create/open daily file
  [ j ] create journal entry 
  [ n ] create blog entry 
  "
    ("b" aws/switch-to-buffer :exit t)
    ("d" my/create-daily-file-or-open-it :exit t)
    ("j" my/create-journal-entry :exit t)
    ("n" my/create-blog-entry :exit t)
    ) 
#+end_src
